tells: US 10Y after the 20:30 SGT payrolls release: back above ~5.29% (Thursday's prior close) = hawkish branch; below ~5.20% = relief branch
Memory (MU, SNDK, SKHY) at the open: if they turn green and lead, the gap is building; if they stay red while chipmakers carry SOXX, the gap is thin

SOXX first-hour volume vs its 10-day average: a gap on light volume that drifts is a hold, one on heavy volume is a build

semis.why: SOXX +1.56% pre (15/18 up, no volume) is already holding the good news: oil -4% on Europe reserve-release talks, the 10Y off its high Thursday, and a strong European regular session in power chips/equipment (Infineon +5.4% on an Oddo upgrade, Aixtron +4.8%, Soitec +4.4%). The traded Asia chip markets did not add (TSMC Taiwan flat, Samsung -0.3%, Hynix +0.6%) and memory, the cycle's leader, is flat-to-red pre-market, so the Micron read-through looks spent. SOXX +6.9% over its 20-day with payrolls an hour after the log: two-sided, with ADP 90k and claims 197k tilting toward a solid figure. Hot payrolls did not stop chips on 09-04, so the rate channel is weak; expect the gap to hold, not build. Diverges from the gap sign on purpose (spec 13)

big_tech.why: QQQ +0.64% pre, all 5 up, led by Palantir/Microsoft +0.8-0.9%, on 0.79x volume; less stretched than chips (median +5.8% vs 50d, QQQ +2.2% vs 20d). Nothing name-specific large; Google ad-tech proposed final judgment due today is behavioural, not structural. Payrolls decides the day; central case the gap holds

market.why: S&P futures +0.48%; SPY flat over 5 days and at its 20-day average; VIX 15.9 in contango; oil relief is in the futures already; Nike -10% after results is a small drag. In-line payrolls (~84-100k, 4.1%) = little to move it; a miss either way moves it past the band

sg_banks.why: STI -0.64% today (5d -1.3%, 1.5x volume Thursday) but the three banks only -0.2% median, so the index weakness was not the banks; Hang Seng -2.7% over two sessions was the regional drag. Monday's close rests on tonight's US close and weekend Iran/diesel headlines; higher US yields support bank margins and the funding-cost argument offsets it. No bank-specific catalyst before the MAS statement (by Oct 14)

summary.bottom_line: Hold what you have and don't add before tonight's US jobs report at 8:30pm SGT. The overnight gains already price in cheaper oil and easier bond yields; the jobs figure decides whether they hold or slip, and my central case is that they hold.
summary.where_we_are: Friday 7:35pm SGT (7:35am in New York). US futures are trading; the US market opens at 9:30pm SGT. Singapore is closed until Monday. Tonight: the US September jobs report at 8:30pm SGT. Nothing scheduled over the weekend.
summary.macro_attribution: Oil moved most since Thursday's US close: US crude is down about 4% to $89 (prices) after reports that the EU discussed releasing more diesel and crude from emergency stocks (Reuters via Investing.com, 2 Oct). The 10-year US Treasury yield also eased on Thursday, to 5.24% from near a 24-year high (prices). The leans do not rest on oil, because that relief is already in the pre-market prices. They rest on tonight's jobs figure.
what_happened: European makers of power chips and chip equipment had a strong session with normal volume behind it: Infineon +5.4%, Aixtron +4.8%, Soitec +4.4% (prices). Infineon also got a broker upgrade from Oddo BHF (Investing.com, 2 Oct).

Asia closed mixed. Korea was +0.5% and Taiwan +0.4%, but TSMC itself was flat in Taiwan. Japan fell 1.2% and Hong Kong 2.7% across two days, because Hong Kong was shut on Thursday (prices). Asia's big chip stocks did not join the rally.
Singapore's STI fell 0.6%, but the three banks slipped only 0.2% (prices), so the index's weakness came from elsewhere.

US futures are up about 0.5% for the S&P 500 and 0.6% for the Nasdaq. Chip stocks are up 1.6% before the open with 15 of 18 higher, led by chipmakers (Intel +2.1%, Nvidia +1.7%), while memory makers are flat to slightly down (prices). Pre-market trades carry no volume, so these gains are not confirmed until the open.
Analysts expect about 90,000 to 100,000 new jobs and unemployment unchanged at 4.1% (Bloomberg, 26 Sep; Yahoo Finance, 2 Oct). Private payrolls from ADP came in at 90,000 (Bloomberg, 30 Sep).

per_group.semis: Chips: flat from here. The 1.6% pre-market rise already contains the oil and yield relief and Europe's chip rally. Asia's chip markets did not add to it, and memory makers, which have led this run, are lagging, so I expect the move to hold rather than grow. The jobs figure will swing chips more than any other group, in either direction.
per_group.big_tech: Big tech: flat from here. It is up 0.6% before the open with all five names higher, and it is less stretched than chips. There is no big company news; Google has a court filing due today in its ad-tech case, where the judge has already ruled out a forced sale of its ad businesses (catalysts.json GOOG).
per_group.market: Whole market: flat from here. S&P futures are up 0.5%, the index is at its 20-day average and the fear gauge (VIX) is low at 15.9 (prices). A jobs figure close to expectations leaves it near where it opens.
per_group.sg_banks: Singapore banks (Monday's close): flat. The banks held up better than the STI today. Monday depends on how the US closes tonight and on weekend Iran and diesel headlines.

change_my_mind: The 10-year yield climbs back above about 5.29% after the jobs figure. Chips would then likely give back their morning gains, which flips chips to slightly down.
The 10-year yield falls below about 5.20% on a weak jobs figure. That is relief, and chips and the whole market would likely build on the morning: slightly up.
Memory makers (Micron, SanDisk, SK Hynix) turn green after the open and lead on heavy volume. The rally would then be widening, not fading, which flips chips to slightly up.
Oil climbs back toward $93 because Europe's reserve release stalls. That flips the whole market to slightly down.
summary.confidence: the jobs figure lands an hour after this read and can cut either way, and a jobs day often moves more than the half-percent range that counts as flat.
summary.cant_know: What the jobs figure will be, and whether markets read a strong one as good news for growth or as a reason for more rate rises.
summary.the_call: Flat. Expect the market to finish close to where it opens, within about half a percent (mild). Chips swing the most either way around the jobs figure, and Singapore banks move the least.
